methods.summary: Image tokens — `(sample_size / patch_size)^2`, 256 for every release.

methods.name: swiglu_hidden_size
methods.summary: SwiGLU inner width: two thirds of `hidden * mlp_ratio`, rounded up to 32.

The release computes `int(2/3 * int(hidden * mlp_ratio))` and then

members.summary: Configuration for the Drifting Model family.

parameters.name: sample_size
parameters.description:
Side of the generated field — the official `input_size`.  `32`
for the SD-VAE latent models, `256` for the pixel models.

parameters.name: in_channels
parameters.description:
Channels of the noise and of the output.  The generator maps a
noise field to a sample of the same shape, so they must match.

parameters.name: out_channels
parameters.description:
Channels of the noise and of the output.  The generator maps a
noise field to a sample of the same shape, so they must match.

parameters.name: patch_size
parameters.description:
Tokenisation patch — `2` for `B/2` / `L/2`, `16` for
`B/16` / `L/16`.  Both give 256 tokens.

parameters.name: hidden_size
parameters.description: Transformer width.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Number of blocks.

parameters.name: num_heads
parameters.description: Attention heads.

parameters.name: mlp_ratio
parameters.description: Feed-forward expansion before the SwiGLU two-thirds rule.

parameters.name: cond_dim
parameters.description:
Width of the conditioning vector that drives adaLN and the
in-context tokens.  Every released model sets it equal to
`hidden_size`.

parameters.name: num_classes
parameters.description:
Class vocabulary.  There is no null class: guidance is trained in
by conditioning on $\alpha$, not by label dropout.

parameters.name: noise_classes
parameters.description:
Codebook size of the random *style embeddings* — the discrete half
of the noise.  `0` disables them.

parameters.name: noise_coords
parameters.description:
How many style indices are drawn per sample; their embeddings are
summed into the conditioning vector.

parameters.name: n_cls_tokens
parameters.description: In-context conditioning tokens prepended to the sequence.

parameters.name: use_qknorm
parameters.description: The LightningDiT modernisations the paper adopts (A.2).

parameters.name: use_swiglu
parameters.description: The LightningDiT modernisations the paper adopts (A.2).

parameters.name: use_rope
parameters.description: The LightningDiT modernisations the paper adopts (A.2).

parameters.name: use_rmsnorm
parameters.description: The LightningDiT modernisations the paper adopts (A.2).

parameters.name: attn_fp32
parameters.description:
Run attention in float32 when the model is in a narrower dtype.
`False` for the released latent `B/2` and `L/2`.

parameters.name: use_remat
parameters.description:
Recompute each block on the backward pass instead of storing its
activations.  `True` for the released pixel models.

parameters.name: frequency_embedding_size
parameters.description: Width of the sinusoid the guidance scale is embedded through.

parameters.name: temperatures
parameters.description:
Kernel temperatures $\tau$ (the release's `R_list`).  One
normalised drift per temperature, summed.

parameters.name: gen_per_label
parameters.description: Generated samples per class label, $N_\mathrm{neg}$.

parameters.name: cfg_min
parameters.description: Range of the training-time guidance scale $\alpha$.

parameters.name: cfg_max
parameters.description: Range of the training-time guidance scale $\alpha$.

parameters.name: neg_cfg_pw
parameters.description:
Exponent of the power law $p(\alpha) \propto \alpha^{-k}$ the
scale is drawn from.

parameters.name: no_cfg_frac
parameters.description:
Probability of replacing the drawn scale by `1` (no guidance).
`0.5` for the released `L/2`.

parameters.name: patch_mean_size
parameters.description: Patch sides over which local feature means / stds are pooled (A.5).

parameters.name: patch_std_size
parameters.description: Patch sides over which local feature means / stds are pooled (A.5).

parameters.name: use_mean
parameters.description: Whether each feature map also contributes its global mean / std.

parameters.name: use_std
parameters.description: Whether each feature map also contributes its global mean / std.

parameters.name: every_k_block
parameters.description:
Also take features from every `k`-th residual block of each
stage.  `None` keeps only the stage outputs.

parameters.name: pos_per_sample
parameters.description: Positive (same-class) samples drawn per label, $N_\mathrm{pos}$.

parameters.name: neg_per_sample
parameters.description:
Unconditional real samples drawn per label, $N_\mathrm{unc}$.
`0` trains without guidance negatives.

parameters.name: positive_bank_size
parameters.description: Per-class sample-queue length.

parameters.name: negative_bank_size
parameters.description: Global unconditional queue length.

parameters.name: use_mae
parameters.description:
Compute the loss in the latent- / pixel-MAE feature space.  No trained
encoder is published, so see
`DriftingForImageGeneration.load_feature_encoder`.

parameters.name: use_convnext
parameters.description: Also use ConvNeXt-V2-Base (ImageNet-22k) features.  Pixel models only.

parameters.name: mae_base_channels
parameters.description: MAE ResNet base width $C$; stages are $C, 2C, 4C, 8C$.

parameters.name: mae_layers
parameters.description: Basic blocks per MAE stage — ResNet-34's.

parameters.name: mae_input_patch_size
parameters.description:
Space-to-depth patch applied before the MAE ResNet: `1` for the
32x32x4 latent, `8` for 256x256x3 pixels (giving 32x32x192).

examples:
>>> from lucid.models.generative.drifting import DriftingConfig
>>> config = DriftingConfig()
>>> config.hidden_size, config.depth, config.patch_size
(768, 12, 2)
>>> config.num_patches, config.swiglu_hidden_size
(256, 2048)
notes:
Reference: Deng, Li, Li, Du, and He, *"Generative Modeling via
Drifting"*, [arXiv:2602.04770](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04770), 2026.  Architecture: Appendix A.2 and
Table 8.  Loss: Alg. 2 and Appendices A.5–A.7.

Where Table 8 and the released `configs/gen/*.yaml` disagree, the
release wins, because the authors' checkpoints were trained by it: the
latent `B/2` uses 64 positives per label (Table 8 says 128).

members.name: DriftingForImageGeneration

methods.name: __init__
methods.summary: Initialise the model. See the class docstring for parameters.

methods.name: load_feature_encoder
methods.summary: Build the frozen feature encoder, with random weights.

parameters.name: pretrained
parameters.description:
No trained encoder is published, so `True` raises
`NotImplementedError` before anything is allocated.

returns.description:
The encoder, also stored as `self.feature_encoder`, with every
parameter frozen, on the generator's device and in its dtype.
Called on `(B, C, H, W)` samples it returns the feature sets
the loss is summed over, a dict of `(B, T, D)` tensors keyed by
set name, `"global"` (the raw sample) first.  `forward`
reads it from `self.feature_encoder`, so the return value is
only needed to look at the features.

notes:
The paper's objective is the drifting loss in the feature space of
an encoder trained as an MAE (A.3), and of ConvNeXt-V2 for pixels
(A.4).  A random encoder is a different objective: training runs
end to end against it, which exercises the pipeline, but do not
expect the paper's results from it.  `use_mae=False,
use_convnext=False` drifts in the raw space and needs no encoder.

warns.description:
If the config asks for a learned feature space, which this does
not deliver: see the Notes.

methods.name: make_sample_queues
methods.summary: The two empty sample queues a training loop feeds (A.8's memory banks).

returns.description:
`num_classes` ring buffers of `positive_bank_size` real
samples each, one per class.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> import lucid.models as models
>>> model = models.create_model("drifting_base_2_gen", pos_per_sample=3,
...                             neg_per_sample=2, use_mae=False, sample_size=8,
...                             hidden_size=32, cond_dim=32, depth=1, num_heads=4,
...                             num_classes=10, gen_per_label=4)
>>> positive_queue, unconditional_queue = model.make_sample_queues()
>>> images, labels = lucid.randn(6, 4, 8, 8), lucid.tensor([0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1])
>>> positive_queue.add(images, labels)
>>> unconditional_queue.add(images, lucid.zeros_like(labels))
>>> step = lucid.tensor([0, 1])
>>> positives, negatives = model.draw_training_batch(
...     positive_queue, unconditional_queue, step)
>>> positives.shape, negatives.shape
((2, 3, 4, 8, 8), (2, 2, 4, 8, 8))
>>> model(positives, step, negatives).loss.ndim
0
notes:
Each step, push the real batch into both with `add(samples,
labels)`: `(N, C, H, W)` samples and their `(N,)` integer
labels, all zeros for `unconditional_queue`.  A full buffer
overwrites its oldest entry.  `draw_training_batch` then reads
`pos_per_sample` positives per label and `neg_per_sample`
unconditional negatives from them, which are the `images` and
`negatives` of `forward`.

methods.name: draw_training_batch
methods.summary: Draw what one training step reads from the two queues.

parameters.name: positive_queue
parameters.description: The per-class queue `make_sample_queues` made.

parameters.name: unconditional_queue
parameters.description:
The single-class queue `make_sample_queues` made.  With
`neg_per_sample=0` it is not read, so it need not have been fed.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: `(N_c,)` the classes to train on.

methods.name: forward
methods.signature: forward(images: Tensor, labels: Tensor, negatives: Tensor | None = None, guidance_scale: float | Tensor | None = None)

parameters.name: images
parameters.description:
Positives: `(N_c, N_pos, C, H, W)` real samples of each label,
or `(N_c, C, H, W)` for one each.  At least one is required.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: `(N_c,)` class labels.

parameters.name: negatives
parameters.description:
`(N_c, N_unc, C, H, W)` unconditional real samples (random
classes) — the extra negatives guidance trains with.  `None`,
or `N_unc = 0`, trains without guidance.

parameters.name: guidance_scale
parameters.description:
Guidance scales: a float or 0-d tensor for every label, or
`(N_c,)`.  Drawn from the configured power law when `None`
and negatives are given; `1` when neither is.

returns.description:
The loss, the generated batch, the scales, the per-feature
terms and the raw drift energies.

raises.description:
If the batch is empty, or its tensors do not fit together —
`guidance_scale` included.
If `guidance_scale` is neither a number nor a tensor.

If the config asks for a learned feature space and no encoder has
been built.

notes:
`gen_per_label` samples are generated per label.  Each feature set
gets its own drifting loss, computed independently per label and
location (rows `(label, location)`), against that label's
positives, its own generated batch, and — weighted by
$w = (\alpha - 1)(N_\mathrm{neg} - 1) / N_\mathrm{unc}$ — the
unconditional samples; the terms are summed (Eq. 14).

methods.name: generate
methods.signature: generate(n_samples: int = 1, labels: Tensor | None = None, guidance_scale: float | Tensor = 1.0, temperature: float = 1.0, noise: Tensor | None = None, style_indices: Tensor | None = None, device: str | None = None)

parameters.name: n_samples
parameters.description: How many to draw.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description:
`(n_samples,)` class indices.  Drawn uniformly when `None` —
the model is class-conditional and has no null class.

parameters.name: guidance_scale
parameters.description:
Guidance scale $\alpha$; any value in the trained range
works without retraining.  The paper's best: `1.0` for
`L/2`, `B/16`, `L/16`; `1.1` for `B/2`.

parameters.name: temperature
parameters.description: Multiplier on the Gaussian noise (the release's `temp`).

parameters.name: noise
parameters.description:
`(n_samples, C, H, W)` noise; drawn when absent (and then
scaled by `temperature`).

parameters.name: style_indices
parameters.description: `(n_samples, noise_coords)` style indices; drawn when absent.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Where to draw.  Defaults to the model's device.

returns.description:
`samples` of shape `(n_samples, out_channels, H, W)` — an
SD-VAE latent for the latent models, `[-1, 1]` RGB for the
pixel models.

examples:
A released configuration, shrunk by overrides so it builds quickly:
>>> from lucid.models import create_model
>>> model = create_model("drifting_base_2_gen", sample_size=8, hidden_size=32,
...                      cond_dim=32, depth=1, num_heads=4).eval()
>>> model.generate(3, guidance_scale=1.5).samples.shape
(3, 4, 8, 8)

members.summary: The drifting objective and its one-step sampler.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The variant to build.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.generative.drifting import (
...     DriftingConfig, DriftingForImageGeneration)
>>> config = DriftingConfig(sample_size=8, hidden_size=32, cond_dim=32, depth=1,
...                         num_heads=4, num_classes=10, noise_classes=4,
...                         noise_coords=2, n_cls_tokens=2, gen_per_label=4,
...                         use_mae=False)
>>> model = DriftingForImageGeneration(config)
>>> model(lucid.randn(2, 3, 4, 8, 8), lucid.tensor([0, 1])).loss.ndim
0
>>> model.generate(2, labels=lucid.tensor([3, 7])).samples.shape
(2, 4, 8, 8)
notes:
Reference: Deng, Li, Li, Du, and He, *"Generative Modeling via
Drifting"*, [arXiv:2602.04770](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04770), 2026.  Training is Alg. 1 with the
feature-space loss of Eq. (14) and the guidance of A.7; sampling is
one evaluation of $f_\theta$.

A checkpoint holds the generator alone: about 8.5 GB of encoder at real
size has no place in it, and `from_pretrained` loads strictly into
a model whose encoder is an empty shell.

Train under `lucid.amp.autocast` with `dtype=lucid.bfloat16`
rather than casting the model, which loses optimizer updates (see
`DriftingConfig`).

attributes.name: drifting
attributes.description: The generator — the only trainable network.

attributes.name: feature_encoder
attributes.description:
The frozen $\phi$.  Empty until
`load_feature_encoder` builds it, unless the config drifts
in the raw space (`use_mae=False, use_convnext=False`).  It moves
and casts with the model but is not a child of it, so it is in no
`state_dict`, `parameters()` or `train()` walk.

methods.summary: Class, styles and guidance scale summed into `(B, cond_dim)`.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: `(B,)` class indices.

parameters.name: guidance_scale
parameters.description: `(B,)` guidance scales $\alpha$.

parameters.name: style_indices
parameters.description: `(B, noise_coords)` style indices, unread when `noise_classes=0`.

parameters.description: The dtype of the result.

methods.name: forward
methods.signature: forward(x: Tensor, labels: Tensor, guidance_scale: float | Tensor = 1.0, style_indices: Tensor | None = None)
methods.summary: Map noise to a sample in one evaluation.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description:
`(B, in_channels, H, W)` Gaussian noise (already scaled by the
sampling temperature, if any).

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: `(B,)` class indices.

parameters.name: guidance_scale
parameters.description:
Guidance scale $\alpha$, a scalar or `(B,)`.  `1` is
no guidance.

parameters.name: style_indices
parameters.description:
`(B, noise_coords)` style indices.  Drawn uniformly when
`None`, as the release always does.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The variant to build.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.generative.drifting import DriftingConfig, DriftingModel
>>> config = DriftingConfig(sample_size=8, hidden_size=32, cond_dim=32, depth=1,
...                         num_heads=4, num_classes=10, noise_classes=4,
...                         noise_coords=2, n_cls_tokens=2)
>>> model = DriftingModel(config).eval()
>>> model(lucid.randn(2, 4, 8, 8), lucid.tensor([0, 1])).sample.shape
(2, 4, 8, 8)
notes:
Reference: Deng, Li, Li, Du, and He, *"Generative Modeling via
Drifting"*, [arXiv:2602.04770](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04770), 2026, Appendix A.2 and Table 8.

The conditioning vector is the release's `c_cfg_noise_to_cond`:



$$
c = E_\mathrm{cls}[y] + \sum_{i=1}^{32} E_i[s_i]
    + 0.02\,\mathrm{RMSNorm}\bigl(\mathrm{MLP}(\mathrm{sin}(\alpha))\bigr),
$$

and it drives both adaLN and the 16 in-context tokens, which are
`Linear(c) + cls_embed` prepended before the first block.  RoPE runs
over the flattened sequence, in-context tokens included, as in the
release.

attributes.name: patch_embed
attributes.description: Patch projection; its input is a `(p, p, C)`-ordered patch.

attributes.name: pos_embed
attributes.description:
`(1, num_patches, hidden_size)` — *trainable*, initialised to the
2-D sine-cosine table.

attributes.name: final
attributes.description: Modulated norm and projection back to patches.

members.name: DriftingOutput
members.signature: DriftingOutput(loss: Tensor, samples: Tensor, guidance_scale: Tensor, feature_losses: dict[str, Tensor], drift_energy: dict[str, Tensor] = dict())
members.summary: What a drifting training step reports.
examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.models.generative.drifting import DriftingOutput
>>> out = DriftingOutput(loss=lucid.zeros(()), samples=lucid.zeros(4, 4, 8, 8),
...                      guidance_scale=lucid.ones(1), feature_losses={})
>>> out.samples.shape
(4, 4, 8, 8)

attributes.name: loss
attributes.description:
Sum over feature sets of the mean drifting loss — a scalar whose
value is the normalised drift energy $\lVert\tilde V\rVert^2$.

attributes.name: samples
attributes.description:
`(N_c * gen_per_label, C, H, W)` — the generated batch, grouped
label-major.

attributes.name: guidance_scale
attributes.description: `(N_c,)` — the guidance scale $\alpha$ each label trained at.

attributes.name: feature_losses
attributes.description: The per-feature-set loss terms, keyed as the encoder names them.

attributes.name: drift_energy
attributes.description:
The release's logged diagnostics, one scalar per feature set and
quantity, keyed `"<feature set>/<quantity>"`: `scale` is the mean
target distance the features are normalised by, and `loss_<tau>` is
the raw drift energy $\lVert V_\tau\rVert^2$ at temperature
$\\tau$, before normalisation.  Detached, in the model's
dtype like `loss` (computed in float32 at least).  `loss` is
scale-normalised and so nearly constant (one per temperature, summed);
these energies are what falls toward zero as the generator approaches
the fixed point, so they are the signal to watch for convergence.
Float32 or wider, whatever the batch's dtype.

members.name: drifting_base_2
members.summary: Drifting `B/2` — the Base generator over the 32x32x4 SD-VAE latent.

parameters.name: pretrained
parameters.description:
No checkpoint is published for `drifting_base_2`, so `True` raises

`DriftingConfig` fields to change on the `latent_sota_B`

examples:
>>> from lucid.models import drifting_base_2
>>> config = drifting_base_2().config
>>> config.depth, config.hidden_size, config.patch_size
(12, 768, 2)
notes:
Reference: Deng, Li, Li, Du, and He, *"Generative Modeling via
Drifting"*, [arXiv:2602.04770](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04770), 2026, Table 8 (`B/2, latent`) and
Table 5 — 12 blocks, width 768, 12 heads, 16 in-context tokens,
32 style tokens.  The paper reports FID 1.75 at one evaluation, guidance 1.1.

Reference: Deng, Li, Li, Du, and He, [arXiv:2602.04770](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04770), 2026, Table 8.

summary: Drifting Models — one-step generation by evolving the pushforward in training.
extended:
Deng, Li, Li, Du and He, [arXiv:2602.04770](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04770), 2026.  A generator is trained
toward a frozen, drifted copy of its own samples: attracted by the data,
repelled by the other samples, through an anti-symmetric field that
vanishes exactly when the two distributions agree.  Inference is one
network evaluation, with guidance trained in rather than applied.
citation: Deng, Mingyang, He Li, Tianhong Li, Yilun Du, and Kaiming He. "Generative Modeling via Drifting." arXiv preprint [arXiv:2602.04770](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04770), 2026.
theory:
A generator $f_\theta$ maps noise to samples, $x = f_\theta(\epsilon)$,
and induces the pushforward $q = f_{\theta\#}\,p_\epsilon$.  Training is a
sequence of models, so it is also a sequence of pushforwards $\{q_i\}$; a
Drifting Model governs that sequence directly with a **drifting field**
$V_{p,q}$ that says how each sample should move:



$$
x_{i+1} = x_i + V_{p,q_i}(x_i).
$$

The field is chosen **anti-symmetric**, $V_{p,q} = -V_{q,p}$, which is all
it takes for $q = p \Rightarrow V = 0$: matched distributions are an
equilibrium.  The instantiation is mean-shift attraction toward the data and
repulsion from the current samples,



$$
V_{p,q}(x) = \frac{1}{Z_p Z_q}\,
    \mathbb{E}_{y^+\sim p,\; y^-\sim q}
    \bigl[k(x, y^+)\,k(x, y^-)\,(y^+ - y^-)\bigr],
\qquad k(x, y) = \exp\!\Bigl(-\tfrac{1}{\tau}\lVert x - y\rVert\Bigr),
$$

with the normalisers $Z$ realised as a softmax over the $y$
samples (and, in practice, a second softmax over the batch of $x$).

The fixed point $f_\theta(\epsilon) = f_\theta(\epsilon) + V(f_\theta(\epsilon))$
becomes a regression onto a frozen target,



$$
\mathcal{L} = \mathbb{E}_\epsilon\Bigl\lVert f_\theta(\epsilon) -
    \mathrm{sg}\bigl(f_\theta(\epsilon) + V(f_\theta(\epsilon))\bigr)\Bigr\rVert^2,
$$

whose value is $\mathbb{E}\lVert V\rVert^2$ but whose gradient never passes
through $V$ — back-propagating through a distribution is what the
stop-gradient avoids.

For images the loss is taken in the feature space of a frozen self-supervised
encoder $\phi$ (a ResNet-style MAE, plus ConvNeXt-V2 for pixels), one term
per scale and location, each with its own distance and drift normalisation and
summed over temperatures $\tau \in \{0.02, 0.05, 0.2\}$.  Guidance is a
training-time behaviour: real samples of other classes join the negatives with
a weight set by a sampled scale $\alpha$, the generator is conditioned on
$\alpha$, and inference stays one evaluation.
